22         For its Complaint against Defendants EcoFactor, Inc. (“EcoFactor”), Shayan
23   Habib (“Habib”), and Amos Nathaniel Goldhaber (“Goldhaber”), Plaintiff Scottsdale
24   Insurance Company (“Scottsdale”) states as follows:
25         1.    This is an insurance coverage action seeking declaratory relief pursuant
26   to 28 U.S.C. §§ 2201, 2202, and 1332.
27

28

                                            -1-
            SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
          Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP        Document 1     Filed 01/20/26   Page 2 of 9



1                                              PARTIES
2             2.    Scottsdale is a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the
3    State of Ohio with its principal place of business located in Scottsdale, Arizona.
4             3.    EcoFactor is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business
5    located in Palo Alto, California.
6             4.    Habib is the Chief Executive Officer and a Director of EcoFactor and is
7    a citizen of the State of California.
8             5.    Goldhaber is a Director of EcoFactor and is a citizen of the State of
9    California.
10                               JURISDICTION AND VENUE
11            6.    The Court has jurisdiction over this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §
12   1332(a)(1). There is complete diversity of citizenship between Scottsdale and
13   Defendants, and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000 exclusive of interest and
14   costs.
15            7.    Venue is proper in this district pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1391(b)(1) and
16   (2) because Defendants are citizens of the State of California and a substantial part of
17   the events or omissions giving rise to the claim occurred in this district.
18                                FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
19                                             The Policy
20            8.    Scottsdale issued Business and Management Indemnity Policy No.
21   EKS3489936 to EcoFactor (the “Policy”) effective for the period from July 31, 2023
22   to July 21, 2024 (the “Policy Period”). A copy of the Policy is attached hereto as
23   “Exhibit 1.”
24            9.    Subject to the Policy’s terms, conditions, limitations, exclusions, and
25   endorsements, the Policy provides coverage under an Employment Practices
26   Coverage Section and a Directors and Officers and Company (“D&O”) Coverage
27   Section. (Id. at Declarations, Item 3.)
28

                                               -2-
               SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
          Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP        Document 1     Filed 01/20/26   Page 3 of 9



1             10.   Insuring Clause A(1) of the D&O Coverage Section of the Policy states
2    that Scottsdale shall pay the “Loss” of the “Directors and Officers” for which the
3    “Directors and Officers” are not indemnified by the “Company” and which the
4    “Directors and Officers” have become legally obligated to pay by reason of a
5    “Claim” first made against the “Directors and “Officers” during the Policy Period or,
6    if elected, the “Extended Period,” and reported to Scottsdale pursuant to Section E(1)
7    of the Policy, for any “Wrongful Act” taking place prior to the end of the Policy
8    Period. (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section § A(1).)
9             11.   Insuring Clause A(2) of the D&O Coverage Section of the Policy states
10   that Scottsdale shall pay the “Loss” of the “Directors and Officers” for which the
11   “Company” had indemnified the “Directors and Officers” and which the “Directors
12   and Officers” have become legally obligated to pay by reason of a “Claim” first made
13   against the “Directors and “Officers” during the Policy Period or, if elected, the
14   “Extended Period,” and reported to Scottsdale pursuant to Section E(1) of the Policy,
15   for any “Wrongful Act” taking place prior to the end of the Policy Period. (Ex. 1 at
16   D&O Coverage Section § A(2).)
17            12.   Insuring Clause A(3) of the D&O Coverage Section of the Policy states
18   that Scottsdale shall pay the “Loss” of the “Company” which the “Company” has
19   become legally obligated to pay by reason of a “Claim” first made against the
20   “Company” during the Policy Period or, if elected, the “Extended Period,” and
21   reported to Scottsdale pursuant to Section E(1) of the Policy, for any “Wrongful Act”
22   taking place prior to the end of the Policy Period. (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section §
23   A(3).)
24            13.   “Company” is defined in the Policy as the “Parent Company” (i.e.,
25   EcoFactor) and any “Subsidiary.” (Ex. 1 at General Terms & Conditions §§ B(2) and
26   (7) and Declarations, Item 1.)
27            14.   “Directors and Officers” is defined in the Policy, in relevant part, as any
28   person who was, now is, or shall become a duly elected or appointed director, officer,
                                               -3-
               SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
             Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP    Document 1    Filed 01/20/26   Page 4 of 9



1    or similar executive of the Company, or any member of the management board of the
2    Company,” among other things. (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section § B(4)(a), as
3    amended by Endorsements No. 20, 28, and 37.)
4            15.   “Loss” is defined in the Policy, in pertinent part, as damages, judgments,
5    settlements, pre-judgment or post-judgment interest awarded by a court, and “Costs,
6    Charges and Expenses” incurred by Directors and Officers under Insuring Clauses 1
7    or 2 or the Company under Insuring Clause 3, but does not include, among other
8    things, (i) matters uninsurable under the laws pursuant to which the Policy is
9    construed, among other exceptions; (ii) the cost of any remedial, preventative, or
10   other non-monetary relief, including without limitation any costs associated with
11   compliance with any such relief of any kind or nature imposed by any judgment,
12   settlement, or governmental authority, (iii) any amounts for which the Insured is not
13   financially liable or legally obligated to pay, or (iv) any amounts owed or paid to one
14   or more securities holders of the Company under any written or express contract or
15   agreement. (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section § B(7), as amended by Endorsement No.
16   31.)
17           16.   “Claim” is defined in the Policy, in relevant part, as a civil proceeding
18   against any “Insured” seeking monetary damages or non-monetary or injunctive
19   relief, commenced by the service of a complaint or similar pleading, among other
20   things. (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section § B(1)(c), as amended by Endorsements No.
21   26, 30, and 39.)
22           17.   “Wrongful Act” is defined in the Policy as any actual or alleged error,
23   omission, misleading statement, misstatement, neglect, breach of duty or act allegedly
24   committed or attempted by (a) any of the Directors and Officers, while acting in their
25   capacity as such, or any matter claimed against any Director and Officer solely by
26   reason of his or her serving in such capacity; (b) any of the Directors and Officers,
27   while acting in their capacity as a director, officer, trustee, governor, executive
28   director or similar position of any “Outside Entity” where such service is with the
                                               -4-
               SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
          Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP      Document 1     Filed 01/20/26   Page 5 of 9



1    knowledge and consent of the Company; and (c) the Company, but only with respect
2    to Insuring Clause 3 of the D&O Coverage Section. (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section
3    § B(9).)
4          18.    The Policy states that Scottsdale shall not be liable for Loss under the
5    D&O Coverage Section on account of any Claim for the return by any of the
6    Directors and Officers of any remuneration paid to them without the previous
7    approval of the appropriate governing body of the Company or “Outside Entity,”
8    which payment without such previous approval shall be held to be in violation of law
9    (the “Return of Remuneration Exclusion”). (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section §
10   C(1)(g).)
11         19.    The Policy states that it shall be the duty of Scottsdale and not the duty
12   of the Insureds to defend any Claim. (Ex. 1 at D&O Coverage Section § F(1).)
13                                  The Underlying Action
14         20.    On or about February 9, 2024, Leo Cheung, Edward Dumont, Scott
15   Hublou, Bryan Ko, Robert Koenig, Eric Saltzman, William Sneed, and John
16   Steinberg, derivatively on behalf of EcoFactor, filed a verified stockholder derivative
17   complaint against EcoFactor, Habib, Goldhaber, and others, Case No. 2024-0117, in
18   the Court of Chancery for the State of Delaware (the “Underlying Action”). On or
19   about October 7, 2025, the plaintiffs in the Underlying Action filed a verified second
20   amended and supplemental stockholder direct and derivative complaint against
21   EcoFactor, Habib, Goldhaber, and others, which is the operative complaint in the
22   Underlying Action. A copy of the second amended complaint filed in the Underlying
23   Action is attached hereto as “Exhibit 2.”
24         21.    In the Underlying Action, the plaintiffs allege that, beginning as early as
25   2015, and continuing at the time the Underlying Action was filed, the defendants
26   agreed upon and entered into a scheme between and among themselves to dilute the
27   plaintiffs’ and other stockholders’ ownership interests in EcoFactor. (Ex. 2 ¶ 1.)
28

                                             -5-
             SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
          Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP      Document 1     Filed 01/20/26   Page 6 of 9



1          22.    According to the plaintiffs in the Underlying Action, the defendants (i)
2    improperly and illegally transferred the majority of the ownership interest in
3    EcoFactor to themselves and/or aided and abetted others in such actions, (ii) withheld
4    critical material information concerning the operation of EcoFactor and its highly
5    valuable intellectual property assets (including information related to EcoFactor’s
6    patent enforcement litigation), (iii) improperly usurped corporate benefits and
7    concealed their actions from the plaintiffs and other stockholders in violation of
8    Delaware law and EcoFactor’s Bylaws, and (iv) caused EcoFactor to transfer
9    significant and valuable assets, including parts of certain patents and other valuable
10   intellectual property, to third parties without the plaintiffs’ knowledge or consent.
11   (Ex. 2 ¶¶ 3-4, 23-125.)
12         23.    The second amended complaint in the Underlying Action sets forth the
13   following causes of action against Habib and Goldhaber: (1) breach of fiduciary duty
14   – dilution; (2) breach of fiduciary duty in seizing a corporate opportunity; (3) breach
15   of contract for violating corporate bylaws; and (4) violation of DGCL §205(f) seeking
16   a declaration that the defendants’ alleged attempted ratification of defective corporate
17   actions are not effective. (Ex. 2 ¶¶ 127-146, 156-162, 184-186.)
18                              Scottsdale’s Coverage Position
19         24.    After the Underlying Action was tendered to Scottsdale for coverage
20   under the Policy, on or about March 20, 2024, counsel for Scottsdale sent a letter to
21   EcoFactor indicating that Scottsdale would provide a defense to Defendants in
22   connection with the Underlying Action pursuant to its right and duty to do so under
23   the Policy and subject to a reservation of its rights under the Policy. A copy of the
24   March 20, 2024 letter is attached hereto as “Exhibit 3.”
25         25.    On or about March 18, 2025 and August 29, 2025, counsel for Scottsdale
26   sent additional letters to EcoFactor reminding Defendants of various coverage issues
27   and defenses that limit or preclude coverage for the Underlying Action under the
28

                                             -6-
             SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
          Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP       Document 1     Filed 01/20/26   Page 7 of 9



1    policy. A copy of the March 18, 2025 letter is attached hereto as “Exhibit 4” and a
2    copy of the August 29, 2025 letter is attached hereto as “Exhibit 5.”
3          26.    On or about December 16, 2025, counsel for Defendants sent a letter to
4    counsel for Scottsdale indicating that Defendants disputed Scottsdale’s coverage
5    position. A copy of the December 16, 2025 letter is attached hereto as “Exhibit 6.”
6      COUNT I – DECLARATORY JUDGMENT AS TO UNINSURABLE LOSS
7          27.    Scottsdale hereby adopts by reference the allegations contained in
8    paragraphs 1 through 27 of this Complaint as if fully set forth herein.
9          28.    An actual, present, and justiciable controversy exists concerning whether
10   the Underlying Action seeks covered Loss under the Policy.
11         29.    Scottsdale requests that the Court declare that the Underlying Action
12   seeks uninsurable loss under the Policy in the form of restitution/disgorgement or
13   other amounts that do not constitute “Loss” under the Policy and that, as a result,
14   Scottsdale is not obligated to defend or indemnify Defendants in connection with the
15   Underlying Action.
16    COUNT II – DECLARATORY JUDGMENT AS TO CAL. INS. CODE § 533
17         30.    Scottsdale hereby adopts by reference the allegations contained in
18   paragraphs 1 through 30 of this Complaint as if fully set forth herein.
19         31.    Section 533 of the California Insurance Code states that “[a]n insurer is
20   not liable for loss caused by the willful act of the insured; but he is not exonerated by
21   the negligence of the insured, or of the insured’s agents or others.”
22         32.    An actual, present, and justiciable controversy exists concerning whether
23   Section 533 of the California Insurance Code bars coverage for the Underlying
24   Action under the Policy.
25         33.    Scottsdale requests that the Court declare that Section 533 of the
26   California Insurance code precludes coverage for the Underlying Action under the
27   Policy and, as a result, Scottsdale is not obligated to defend or indemnify Defendants
28   in connection with the Underlying Action.
                                             -7-
             SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
          Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP      Document 1     Filed 01/20/26   Page 8 of 9



1          COUNT III – DECLARATORY JUDGMENT AS TO RETURN OF
2                             REMUNERATION EXCLUSION
3          34.     Scottsdale hereby adopts by reference the allegations contained in
4    paragraphs 1 through 34 of this Complaint as if fully set forth herein.
5          35.     An actual, present, and justiciable controversy exists concerning whether
6    the Policy’s Return of Remuneration Exclusion precludes coverage for the
7    Underlying Action under the Policy.
8          36.     Scottsdale requests that the Court declare that the Return of
9    Remuneration Exclusion precludes coverage for the Underlying Action under the
10   Policy and, as a result, Scottsdale is not obligated to defend or indemnify Defendants
11   in connection with the Underlying Action.
12                                  PRAYER FOR RELIEF
13         WHEREFORE, Scottsdale prays that this Court enter an Order:
14         1.      declaring that the Underlying Action seeks uninsurable loss under the
15   Policy in the form of restitution/disgorgement or other amounts that do not constitute
16   “Loss” under the Policy and that, as a result, Scottsdale is not obligated to defend or
17   indemnify Defendants in connection with the Underlying Action;
18         2.      declaring that Section 533 of the California Insurance Code precludes
19   coverage for the Underlying Action under the Policy and, as a result, Scottsdale is not
20   obligated to defend or indemnify Defendants in connection with the Underlying
21   Action;
22         3.      declaring that the Policy’s Return of Remuneration Exclusion precludes
23   coverage for the Underlying Action under the Policy and, as a result, Scottsdale is not
24   obligated to defend or indemnify Defendants in connection with the Underlying
25   Action;
26         4.      awarding Scottsdale its costs and expenses; and
27

28

                                               -8-
               SCOTTSDALE INSURANCE COMPANY’S COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT
          Case 5:26-cv-00618-PCP    Document 1   Filed 01/20/26   Page 9 of 9



1          5.     awarding Scottsdale all other relief that the Court deems just and
2    equitable.
3

4
